intent: Develop motion from the whole arrangement: establish the low clock, open the first exchange, suspend it, make a compact physical return, transfer the foreground to metal, and resolve into harmonic memory.

rhythmic_grammar.opening: The familiar .75-beat call falls toward D; its depth belongs to the current block.
rhythmic_grammar.recovery: The 1.5-beat response recoils toward D rather than introducing an unrelated turn.
rhythmic_grammar.ground: The cell's last D/A destination holds its pitch. It gives the bass, relay and next call a clear landing.
rhythmic_grammar.reply: Upper metal replies bend in the same field as the call and recover before the next cell.
rhythmic_grammar.suspension: Long arches replace short calls while the fixed D/A/F field carries the harmonic reference.
rhythmic_grammar.metal_foreground: Metal inherits opening/recovery/ground syntax for a complete 16-bar block; the sparse A signal becomes the anchor.
rhythmic_grammar.memory: The foreshadow and closing blocks keep stable pitches; roughness and spatial decay supply their movement.

blocks.name: Physical clock
blocks.context: Kick, engine and drums establish the pulse. Neither melodic voice is present.

blocks.name: Fixed outline
blocks.context: Sparse D arrivals sit beside held field and veil. Keep the tonal outline still before developing it.

blocks.name: First elasticity
blocks.context: The existing kick withdrawal gives the engine space. Call and recovery move as one repeating cell; the closing note holds.

blocks.name: Interlocked exchange
blocks.context: The full drum clock returns. Signal calls and metal replies retain their rhythmic relationship above lower relay entries.

blocks.name: Opening the field
blocks.context: The recurring cell becomes more elastic for the complete block. The held field and veil approach the suspension while its final D/A notes remain grounded.

blocks.name: Suspended orbit
blocks.context: Kick, engine and relay withdraw. Long signal and metal arches move against the stable D/A/F field; returns breathe between foreground attacks.

blocks.name: Physical return
blocks.context: The preferred low clock lands. Compact elastic calls and stable cell endings let its weight lead before the next expansion.

blocks.name: Second expansion
blocks.context: With the low clock established, consecutive cells deepen together. Repeated landings keep the expansion tied to the groove.

blocks.name: Making room
blocks.context: The signal clears space for the coming kick withdrawal and the relay's exposed replies.

blocks.name: Metal approaches
blocks.context: The unchanged engine carries the short kick loss. Metal replies gain elasticity as the relay remains audible.

blocks.name: Passing the current
blocks.context: Returning drums close the space. Metal keeps the developing gesture while the signal stops competing for the foreground.

blocks.name: Metal current
blocks.context: Metal owns the full cell for 16 bars. Its opening and recovery bend; its ending and the sparse A signal hold. Lower relay and veil support the takeover.

blocks.name: Signal rejoins
blocks.context: The signal returns to the opening/recovery syntax. Metal steps back into replies; shared vibration and return rhythm connect their identities.

blocks.name: Releasing the foreground
blocks.context: The score already thins the signal. Reduce excursion and let fixed endings prepare the held closing field.

blocks.name: Residual memory
blocks.context: The machine withdraws in its accepted order. Remaining D arrivals and upper metal hold their destinations while field and veil carry the ending.

provenance: Authored from Study 04 notes, physical voices, full-form activity and the user's listening correction. STRIDULATION informs foreground/support relationships and receding returns. No source recording, measured control curve or reference MIDI enters the performance.
